title: Per-request Adaptive Inference Experimentation Orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a per-request orchestration layer and UX for running controlled A/B experiments, shadow deployments, and canary rollouts that supports automatic statistical checks and safe auto-rollback. The feature will let engineers define per-request routing rules (risk-aware routing), exposure schedules, sequential/bayesian stopping rules, and integrated telemetry for quality and latency regressions.

Background: Teams currently rely on coarse traffic split mechanisms in Console and separate ad-hoc infra for shadowing. This leads to inconsistent signal (due to batching/cache effects), slow experiment cycles (manual sample size calculations), and risky rollouts without standardized early-stop rules. We want a repeatable, low-latency-first experimentation mode that respects production SLOs.

Scope: MVP will include: 1) Experiment manifest format (Declarative experiment spec) supporting per-request filters, exposure targets, and stop conditions; 2) Runtime routing hooks that support sampling, deterministic hashing, and a risk-score gate that can route to shadow/variant while preserving latency SLOs; 3) Sequential statistical checks (Bayesian credible intervals + frequentist optional) integrated with Console to surface early warnings and recommended auto-rollback; 4) Shadow traffic plumbing with opt-in downstream recording and cost budget controls; 5) Integrations with Optimize for sample size suggestions and with Observability for token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

Non-goals for MVP: full cohort bucketing DSL, multi-arm experiments with dynamic allocation (bandit), or model-distillation telemetry. Those are planned for subsequent phases.

Trade-offs:
- Latency vs statistical power: We will limit experiment scope to per-request sampling without additional synchronous validation calls to avoid added tail latency. This reduces sensitivity for rare-failure detection; to compensate we provide a shadow option that records async traces for offline analysis.
- Batching/cache interference: Continuous batching and prefix KV caches can bias per-request metrics. We'll provide instrumentation to mark requests participating in an experiment so the runtime can attempt to isolate them from aggressive batching when requested (at cost of throughput).
- Auto-rollback aggressiveness: Default conservative thresholds (low false-positive risk) for auto-rollback, with an opt-in aggressive mode for teams that prefer quick reverts.

Stakeholders and approvers: Product (Maya Chen), Runtime Eng (Samir Rao), Console UX (Aisha Patel), SRE (Daniel Greer), Research/Stats (Ellen Park).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create an experiment manifest via Console or API with per-request selectors and exposure target.
Runtime applies routing decisions for at least 10k qps config in dedicated staging without >5% tail-latency increase for non-participating traffic.
Sequential statistical checks run every sampling window and surface a pass/warn/fail state in Console; documented default thresholds and rationale provided.
Shadow traffic can be recorded asynchronously and replayed for offline evals; storage budget and opt-out controls respected.
Auto-rollback triggers when preset severity conditions are met and a rollback runbook is executed with annotated audit logs and incident ticket creation.
Integrations: Optimize provides sample-size guidance for the experiment; Observability dashboard surfaces variant-level latency, error-rate, and cost-per-token by model version.
updates: 2026-02-22 — Initial scoping workshop. Decision: use a single experiment manifest schema that covers per-request routing and shadowing instead of separate artifacts. Action: ENG to draft schema (ENG-4122).

2026-02-28 — Runtime feasibility review with Samir. Found that deterministic hashing plus risk-score gating is simplest to implement with existing routing. Identified implementation risk: KV-cache isolation will require a new flag in runtime (ENG-4298).

2026-03-03 — Stats review with Ellen: recommended default sequential test: Bayesian posterior probability that variant error-rate > control by delta threshold, and a frequentist optional p-value check. Ellen to provide priors and threshold doc. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Experiment+Statistical+Guidelines

2026-03-05 — UX review: Console needs a lightweight experiment overview card and a full experiment timeline view. Aisha provided wireframes and noted visibility requirements for audit logs. Wireframes stored in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-experiment-wires

2026-03-09 — Prototype PR opened for manifest parsing and routing hooks: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7321. Basic e2e in staging passes for 1k qps with shadowing enabled. Performance note: enabling cache-isolation increased per-token cost by ~7% in staging.

2026-03-12 — Decision: ship conservative auto-rollback defaults (min sample 5000, posterior>0.99 and delta>1.5x error-rate) and allow project-level tuning. Added follow-up task to document rollback runbook and alerting thresholds (PM-880322). Blockers: SRE wants scripted incident creation integration (ENG-4410).
